subject.title: Onboarding Wizard should include Memory/Embedding setup as a mandatory step

question: Should first-run onboarding and openclaw configure treat memory embedding setup as mandatory, prominently optional, or diagnostic-only, and what credential/probe UX should it use?
rationale: The missing setup surface is clear in current main, but requiring embeddings changes first-run completion, provider cost/network assumptions, SecretRef/plaintext handling, daemon environment expectations, and FTS-only workflows, so automation should not choose the policy.

options.title: Prominent Optional Setup
options.body: Add a visible but skippable memory setup/readiness step that writes existing memorySearch provider/model and SecretRef or API-key config, then points users to memory status verification.

options.title: Mandatory Memory Gate
options.body: Require users to configure embeddings or explicitly choose FTS-only before onboarding completes, improving recall readiness at the cost of first-run friction and provider dependency.

options.title: Diagnostic Only
options.body: Keep onboarding lean and rely on doctor, memory status, and documentation, accepting that some users may miss memory readiness until after setup.

recommendation.title: Prominent Optional Setup
recommendation.body: Add a visible but skippable memory setup/readiness step that writes existing memorySearch provider/model and SecretRef or API-key config, then points users to memory status verification.

likelyOwner.reason: Takhoffman is the current issue assignee and participated in the product-scope discussion on this exact setup behavior.
